escena: SCENE (cinematic, Hollywood blockbuster still, bullet time, a dark film studio at night): a Latin American art director in his late thirties, short dark hair and a trimmed beard, wearing the Efeonce hoodie exactly as in its reference, stands slightly RIGHT of center in the lower part of the frame, framed from the waist up, looking straight into the lens with calm, precise focus. In front of him, at chest height and slightly to his right, floats a fictitious faceted glass perfume bottle with NO label and NO lettering, frozen in time in the middle of a splash: amber liquid and hundreds of clear droplets hang perfectly still in mid-air around it. With the fine tip of a thin silver stylus held in his right hand he touches ONE single droplet, nudging it a millimetre into place: the only intervention in the frozen instant. Behind the bottle, EXACTLY SIX thin translucent film frames of light float in a gentle arc like a filmstrip receding into depth, each showing the same splash at a successive instant, the nearest one sharp and the last one melted into the haze. LIGHT: one hard warm orange (#FF6500) key light is born inside the splash, refracting through the bottle and the droplets: it is the brightest element of the frame and lights his face, his hand and the stylus from below; NO fill light, the far side of his face in deep shadow. A cool azure (#0375DB) rim light from behind outlines his head and shoulders; haze catches the refracted orange light. REALISTIC ADULT PROPORTIONS: camera about two meters away at chest height, 85mm at f/2, nothing foreshortened, he does not lean toward the lens. The TOP 30% of the frame is calm, deep dark studio space with only faint haze, no droplets, no frames, no objects; everything stays below 34% of the frame height. Enormous contrast, deep navy blacks, punchy, awe-inspiring. No readable text, no letters, no logos of any brand.
